answers.workaround:
There are a few ways to work around this, but they feel a bit clunky to me.

You can immediately check the value returned to see if it's an empty string, and if so, set it to the default instead:
```gdscript
var sound_name = parser.get_named_attribute_value_safe("name")
if sound_name == "": sound_name = "beep"
```
This may cause issues if the user intends to explicitly pass an empty string as the parameter value, although I haven't run into this in my own projects.

Alternatively, you can construct a dictionary out of the attributes, then use the `Dictionary.get()` method on it:
```gdscript
var attributes = {}
for i in parser.get_attribute_count():
    attributes[parser.get_attribute_name(i)] = parser.get_attribute_value(i)
    
var sound_name = attributes.get("name", "beep")
```
This proposal is essentially suggesting the implementation of `Dictionary.get()` for named attributes.

title: Add optional argument for default return value to `XMLParser.get_named_attribute_value_safe()`
